summary.text: St. Philip, one of the Seven, preaches in Samaria and explains Isaiah to the Ethiopian official in Acts. He is distinct from Philip of the Twelve.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

saints.context: The source’s received ecclesiastical narrative is identified as such. Uncertain dates, later traditions and unknown circumstances of death are retained as uncertain.

blocks.text: Acts names St. Philip among the seven chosen when the Jerusalem community addresses the distribution of food to widows. He later becomes a preacher in Samaria after persecution disperses the believers. His identity is distinct from the Apostle of the Twelve with the same name.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: On the road toward Gaza, he approaches an Ethiopian official who is reading Isaiah. Asked about the passage, St. Philip explains Jesus from the text and baptizes the official. Acts later places him at Caesarea, calls him the evangelist and one of the Seven, and mentions his four daughters who prophesy.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The OCA’s received account says that St. Philip later served as bishop in Tralles in Asia Minor and died in old age. Those details are distinguished from the canonical Acts narrative. The account does not describe his death as martyrdom.
blocks.locator: Final paragraph on later ministry and death

blocks.text: The OCA commemorates him on October 11 as an Apostle of the Seventy and one of the Seven Deacons. Its opening sentence expressly distinguishes him from Philip of the Twelve, whose commemoration is November 14.
